overview: The Council enacted a leaf blower restriction ordinance and approved a resolution pressing the MBTA to remove creosote-treated railroad ties stored along residential rail lines. It also held extensive debates regarding city infrastructure backlogs, water department management, and fire department staffing and consulting costs.

items.title: Approval of Minutes and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved the records of the April 2 meeting alongside committee reports on the police body-worn camera pilot program and a zoning work plan prepared by Innes Associates.

items.title: Resolution Recognizing National Animal Therapy Day
items.summary: Suspended rules and adopted a resolution designating April 30 as National Animal Therapy Day and requesting a mayoral proclamation.

items.title: Resolution on Water Department Concerns
items.summary: Placed on file following extensive discussion on aging infrastructure, long-term rate studies, and the resignation letter of the former water superintendent.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Former councilor and state representative Cavanaugh addressed the council to honor Jack McGlynn's World War II service in the Ghost Army, followed by public comments on road conditions, council meetings, and decorum.

items.title: Resolution on Lawsuit Settlements and Investigations Reporting
items.summary: Referred to the mayor requesting an accounting of legal settlements and expenditures, as well as an executive session with the council.

items.title: Resolutions on Creosote MBTA Railroad Ties
items.summary: Adopted joined resolutions urging the MBTA to immediately remove creosote-soaked railroad ties stored adjacent to residences and requesting the material safety data sheet.

items.title: Resolution on Fire Department Outside Consultant and Staffing
items.summary: Requested an explanation from the mayor regarding why the city's FEMA staffing grant application sought funding for 11 firefighters rather than 15, amidst debate over hiring an outside consultant to review department policies.

items.title: Resolution on Krystle Campbell Peace Garden Maintenance
items.summary: Referred to the DPW commissioner to arrange discussions between city officials and the garden's trust to address funding and repairs needed for the memorial fountain.

items.title: Personnel Ordinance Amendment: Supervisor of Water and Sewer
items.summary: Tabled to April 30 while requesting clarification from the administration and legal counsel regarding whether voting on the reclassification is impacted by pending union arbitration.

items.title: Leaf Blower Ordinance Final Passage
items.summary: Ordained the leaf blower restriction ordinance on its third reading following public comments regarding its scope and advertising.

items.title: Reports Due and Council Communications
items.summary: Voted to place five expired reporting matters on file and heard member remarks regarding meeting civility and decorum following a resident email.
